subject: Stitching decision path + internal ammo for FinexCorp pilot
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alicia Bennett <alicia.bennett@finexcorp.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + proposal for next 2 weeks (pilot checklist)

Hi Alicia — great to meet your team on the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

What we covered
- Pilot scope: 2 teams (fraud ops + customer support), ~500k tokens/day projection, 3-week evaluation window.
- Security: standard SOC2 controls, options for VPC deployment, data residency discussion flagged for procurement.
- Success metrics: average inference latency under 120ms, 20% reduction in time-to-resolution on support triage, and per-token cost below $0.0025 on committed capacity.

Asks / open items for FinexCorp
1) Introduce the CISO or security review lead for a short sync (we need to confirm data flow and KMS approach) — you mentioned Tom Rivers as the likely owner.
2) Procurement checklist: standard SOW timeline and PO cadence, any preferred contract terms we should preempt.
3) Decision criteria: confirm who the economic buyer will be and the internal timeline for procurement approval.

What we’ll deliver this week
- A two‑slide ROI snapshot for the fraud ops use case. (Marissa is looping in.)
- SOC2 summary + short VPC deployment note (attached).
- Pilot mutual action plan draft with dates and owners.

Proposed next steps
- Security intro call with Tom (20–30 min) — can we do Tue/Wed next week?
- Procurement touchpoint: Alicia to share procurement contact; we’ll send a one‑page procurement checklist.

I’ll follow up internally to pull the ROI and pricing pieces together — copying Marissa and Priyom to help prepare the internal materials. Thanks again for the time today.

Best,
Soojin

Thanks, Soojin — good session. Quick answers:

- I’ve looped Tom (CISO) and our procurement alias. Tom can do Wed 08/25 at 10am PT for a 30-minute security sync.
- Procurement: Our standard SOW window is 30–45 days once legal signs off; for pilots we often accept a shorter agreement (MOU + PO). Procurement will send standard redlines but can fast-track if we have an exec sponsorship email.
- Economic buyer is likely our VP Product, Heather Lawson. Heather will want clear ops KPIs and expected cost offsets.

I’ll ask procurement to share the contact details and any standard template. Looking forward to the ROI slide.

—Alicia

1) Marissa: ROI snapshot (1–2 slides) focused on fraud ops — please include: baseline metrics assumptions, modeled agent-hours saved, and an ASP-based cost offset table we can show to Heather Lawson. Target: 1 slide + 1 appendix table.

2) Priyom: Pragmatic pilot pricing and a short procurement cheat-sheet (one page) showing contract options: MOU + PO path, short SOW, and an estimated monthly committed rate vs burst. Call out SOC2/VPC as optional add-ons and expected uplift.

We have a Wed 10am PT security call with Tom — attach SOC2-summary.pdf and a 2‑paragraph VPC note. I’ll draft a mutual action plan after we have the ROI/pricing stubs.

Quick notes to include in the materials: decision criteria: security signoff, VP Product economic OK, and a pilot success signal (>=15% reduction in manual review FPR or 20% faster TTR).

Thanks — Soojin

Got it — I put together an ROI one-pager and a 2-slide summary for Heather that emphasizes the economic levers. Attached: redwood-pilot-map.xlsx (slide + model) and a short pricing snapshot as PDF.

Highlights included in the ROI:
- Assumptions: 500k tokens/day, 3 agents equivalent saved per 100k tokens for fraud triage, agent cost $65/hr.
- Modeled 18% reduction in human triage time (conservative), leading to an estimated $46k/month ops savings in the scope described.
- Breakeven within 2 months on committed rate under the proposed pilot terms.

I added a slide that maps the internal stakeholders and recommended talk tracks: Heather (economic buyer) — focus on ops savings and time-to-value; Tom (security) — highlight SOC2, VPC option, limited data retention; Procurement — propose MOU + 30-day PO with exec sponsorship.

I also flagged a few sensitive items for Priyom to call out in the procurement cheat-sheet: encryption key management, audit log retention, and DPA terms.

Attaching: redwood-pilot-map.xlsx, pilot-pricing-proposal.pdf

—Marissa
